newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus denies it seeks removal of French diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus denies it seeks removal of French diplomat.

text.p: The Cypriot government on Friday denied a newspaper report that it had sought the removal of the French ambassador because of a perceived pro-Turkish stance on the conflict splitting the island.

In a terse four-line statement, the government press and information office dismissed the front-page report in the right-wing Greek Cypriot daily Agon suggesting they asked the France to "quickly and quietly" replace ambassador Henri Jacolin.

Agon - whose publisher is a cabinet member - said the government lodged strong protests to the French Foreign Ministry over a private visit of Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash to Paris last week during which he had contacts with a high-ranking foreign ministry official.
Such a meeting, Agon said, was considered tantamount to recognition of the breakaway state Denktash heads in northern Cyprus. The paper said Jacolin had helped arrange Denktash's visit.

"It is clarified that the Cyprus government has not asked for the removal of the French ambassador in Nicosia," the government statement said, without saying if it had made a protest over Denktash's visit.
Officials of the French embassy in Nicosia were not immediately available for comment.

Denktash heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state recognised only by Ankara in northern Cyprus, occupied by Turkey in 1974 in the wake of a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military ruling Greece.
The Greek Cypriot-led government in the south enjoys international recognition.
